test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 9 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is a good way to measure the population density of fishes found in lakes?

options.text: The number of fish caught per trap

solution:
The correct answer is__** The number of fish caught per trap.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The population density of a fish in a lake can be measured by **the number of fish per trap in the lake**.
 
• The three types of age pyramids are **Expanding, Stable, and declining**. 
 
• A stable age pyramid is also known as** a 'bell-shaped' pyramid.**
 
• In this type of pyramid, the** pre and post-reproductive populations are the same.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/644410333e549872b4fc6222ded6aa9f1f88dccb7bf8f8af7eed5f7fd25ec350.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Figures described by Sjögren reflected an average tadpole survival rate of **1 – 2 %**, while other studies estimated that** tadpole survival rates **may **average at around 1%.**
 
• The density of O2 is **16 kg/m3** at NTP.
 
• Zooplankton can reproduce rapidly, and **populations can increase by about 30 per cent a day under favourable conditions**.
 
• Zooplankton reaches maturity quickly and **lives short, but productive lives.**
